unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Let $X_l$, $l\in\mathbb N$, be independent copies of a non-standard regularly varying $[0,\infty)^d$-valued random vector $X$. Assume that the vector $X^*=(r_1^{-1}X_1^\alpha,\ldots,r_d^{-1}X_d^\alpha)$ satisfies Eq. (3) and (30). Let $\{k_n\}_{n\in\mathbb N}\subset\mathbb N$ be a sequence such that $k_n\to\infty$, $k_n/n\to0$ and $\sqrt{k_n}A_i^*(n/k_n)\to0$ for all $1\le i\le d$.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Using the same techniques as in the proof of Cor. 6, one can easily show the joint weak convergence of $(G_n(v,s,\beta,p_1),\widetilde G_n(w,t,\gamma,p_2))_{n\in\mathbb N}$ ($v,s,\beta,p_1$), ($w,t,\gamma,p_2$) in $\partial B_1^+(0)\times A'_\delta\times K$ to $(G(v,s,\beta,p_1),\widetilde G(w,t,\gamma,p_2))$ which are jointly Gaussian. Then for $\beta=\gamma=\mathbf1$, the covariances express as
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(G(v,s,\mathbf1,p_1),\widetilde G(w,t,\mathbf1,p_2))
=\frac{\mathbb E\left[\left(v^\top\frac{s\circ\Theta}{\|s\circ\Theta\|}\right)^{p_1}\left(w^\top\frac{t\circ\Theta}{\|t\circ\Theta\|}\right)^{p_2}(\|s\circ\Theta\|\wedge\|t\circ\Theta\|)\right]}{\mathbb E[\|t\circ\Theta\|]}
\]
\[
-\frac{\mathbb E\left[\left(v^\top\frac{s\circ\Theta}{\|s\circ\Theta\|}\right)^{p_1}(\|s\circ\Theta\|\wedge\|t\circ\Theta\|)\right]\mathbb E\left[\left(w^\top\frac{t\circ\Theta}{\|t\circ\Theta\|}\right)^{p_2}\|t\circ\Theta\|\right]}{(\mathbb E[\|t\circ\Theta\|])^2}.
\]

This is original covariance context for D26, not a proof-only dependency or an assumption of independence.

source_issues.note: Registered local source is arXiv:2010.03832v2 marked3Jul2024, with running preprint dateJuly4,2024. Main text and acknowledgements end on PDFpage25; clip at y520 before References y527.295. AppendixA begins26. Exactly Theorems5,8,10 are inventoried; Corollary6 is retained only for its explicit assumption import and Gaussian definition.

Section2 prints E=[0,infinity)^d while vague regular variation normally needs an origin-excluded cone or equivalent topology. Eq3 states a*(u)~1/P(X_i*>u); the Section3.2 prose instead prints a*(.)~P(X_i*>.), apparently missing the inverse. Use Eq3 as the defining normalization and preserve the discrepancy. The model has asymptotically normalized margins, not necessarily exact standard Pareto margins.

Section2 and Section3.2 standardize each coordinate using alpha_i, whereas Theorem8 prints X_i^alpha with an unindexed exponent. Theorem8’s Gaussian covariance still uses alpha_i alpha_j. Preserve the theorem verbatim and the original model separately; do not silently impose equal indices or repair the displayed theorem.

The printed A_delta,I lies in (0,infinity)^d but also requires zero coordinates off I. Literally proper-support strata are empty. The surrounding discussion intends masked nonnegative scaling vectors close to1_I. Keep the printed set and record the apparent orthant error, rather than redefining it. This affects the domain of the process and derivative statements.

Corollary6 condition(27) prints tau E||s circle X*|| c and v in partial B1*(0), whereas Eq23/26 use the spectral Theta and the plus simplex. The starred B1 domain is not defined. The X* expectation differs from the bounded spectral normalization and can be infinite, for example with standard Pareto margins. Index1 regular variation alone does not force its mean to be infinite. Preserve both expressions; this is an unresolved source discrepancy in an assumption explicitly imported by Theorem10.

Theorem5 centers at the exact finite-sample expectation and does not assume Eq27 or Eq30. Theorem8 imports Eq3/30 and the coordinatewise second-order bias rate, but not Corollary6’s angular bias assumption. Theorem10 explicitly imports both Corollary6 and Theorem8 assumptions. A reference to the Gaussian limit object alone does not import every assumption or conclusion of its originating result.

The simplex is nonnegative with l1 norm1, but v_I masks coordinates without renormalizing, so v_I need not lie in that simplex. Theorem10 evaluates c and Gaussian processes at v_I nonetheless. The formulas extend homogeneously, but the extension is not explicitly stated. Likewise all coordinate partial derivatives on stratified A_delta prime require an extension/relative convention at inactive zeros and boundary points. Record these issues rather than altering the domain.

The source specifies0^0=1 for Phat, but does not fully state zero-angle or zero-exceedance-denominator conventions. Theta/ell_I(Theta) under the tilted spectral law can be undefined on zero-weight angles; the integral needs a harmless convention there. Order-statistic ratios assume positive denominators. Strict exceedances above the kth upper order statistic can give k−1 observations in a continuous sample and fewer with ties; do not replace Ptilde by k/n or add an unstated no-tie hypothesis.

Theta^I is an ell_I(Theta)-tilted angular law, not simple rescaling under the original probability. Theorem8’s tau_ij is the {i,j} subset coefficient, while tau is the full-set coefficient. Remark7.1 uses projected Theta_I^I. These probability laws and constants remain separate even though linked by Eq14–15.

Theorem10’s Gtilde,G^0 and Htilde are jointly coupled limits. Preserve Remark7.2’s G/Gtilde cross covariance, Eq34’s H/G covariance and the i in J zero H/Gtilde covariance. G^0 is the p=0 restriction of G. The general Gtilde covariance Eq48 is in an excluded appendix, but Remark7.1 gives the needed s=1_I,beta=1 specialization in full; do not read the appendix or assume independence of all components.

Equation35 prints Theta_i wedge Theta_J in a scalar covariance expression without a norm around the vector Theta_J. Its interpretation is ambiguous. Theorem10 only needs i in I, for which the following original sentence explicitly states zero H_i/Gtilde covariance. Retain that clean specialization and note the unresolved general expression, without silently correcting it.

Theorem10’s display uses k whereas its assumptions use k_n; preserve this notation and record k=k_n along the stated sequence. Finiteness of K is inherited from Corollary6. The Hill prose uses alpha_hat_{k,n,i} while(33) uses alpha_hat_{n,k,i}. Rem7.2 states K although its zeroth-moment specialization is used later; G at p=0 is explicitly defined in Theorem5 and before Theorem10. No source notation is silently rewritten.

ambient_conventions: Nonnegative real d-vectors; maximum norm unless norm1 is specified; coordinatewise powers, products and ratios; indicator vectors and masked coordinates; scalar minima and coordinate subset maxima.

Unit Pareto radial Y has survival1/y for y≥1 and is independent ofTheta. The normalized probability spectral law is distinct frommu* andtau. Vague and weak convergence, bounded-function l-infinity spaces, tightness and centered Gaussian laws retain standard ambient meanings.

All estimator definitions preserve finite-sample strict exceedances and original power/order indices. The denominator A3 is available independently of the Hill numerator, avoiding a circular graph. No mathlib availability is inferred.

I and J are nonempty coordinate subsets where their maxima are used. Tau_ij denotes tau_{i,j}; repeated indices reduce to a singleton. The source does not explicitly discuss every zero-division convention, extension domain or tie case.

Original multi-location excerpts in D10,D23,D26 and A4 preserve the cited pieces without presenting them as one contiguous source paragraph. Eq48 and all appendix bodies are excluded. This audit records statements and dependencies; it does not prove them or repair the source.
